Let $\beta>0$ and $\Gamma>0$. For a real shift $\nu$ of the lead occupation the occupation-weighted
Lorentzian integrates to a digamma function,
\begin{equation}
\int d\omega\, \frac{n_F(\omega+\nu)}{\omega^2+\Gamma^2} = \frac{\pi}{2\Gamma} - \frac{1}{2i\Gamma}\left[\psi\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\beta(\Gamma+i\nu)}{2\pi}\right)-\psi\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\beta(\Gamma-i\nu)}{2\pi}\right)\right] .
\label{eq:real}
\end{equation}
For the bosonic Matsubara frequency $\Omega = 2\pi/\beta$ we continue $\nu \to i\Omega$,
\begin{equation}
\int d\omega\, \frac{n_F(\omega+i\Omega)}{\omega^2+\Gamma^2} = \frac{\pi}{2\Gamma} - \frac{1}{2i\Gamma}\left[\psi\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\beta(\Gamma-\Omega)}{2\pi}\right)-\psi\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\beta(\Gamma+\Omega)}{2\pi}\right)\right] .
\label{eq:imag}
\end{equation}
